pricing_details.methodology_language: Olympus methodology language is technical and empirical; PropLine documents a free request quota, deterministic odds conversion, no-vig cross-book +EV and graded outcomes. Detailed competitor model methodologies are generally NOT CONFIRMED on the assigned pricing pages.

methodology_and_algorithms.description: Olympus describes a nine-step pipeline: ingest schedule/odds/injury/metrics data; league-specific Monte Carlo; Platt and per-league isotonic calibration; edge; 15-dimensional profitability zones; adaptive regime threshold; Kelly sizing after probability shrinkage; append-only ledger; automatic resolution and calibration feedback. PropLine says prices pass through unchanged, decimal odds are computed deterministically, and cross-book +EV uses a no-vig fair line with Pinnacle preferred and Bovada fallback.
methodology_and_algorithms.engine_versions: Olympus page labels NBA Possession Monte Carlo v5.0.2-calibrated-possession; NHL Pinnacle v19.1-pinnacle; CBB Savant Ultra v5.0.1; NFL Elite Pinnacle v1.1; MLB Pitch Sim v5.0; Soccer PBP v16.3; LoL Championship v2.1; Golf Conditional Sim v3.2; Tennis V2 (calibrating); Olympic Hockey v2.2.

key_formulas.value: Edge = calibrated probability minus market-implied probability; methodology reports typical minimum-edge floors of 3–8 percentage points.
Kelly sizing is applied after 15% Bayesian probability shrinkage toward 50%.
Platt scaling uses regularization C=10.0; reported Brier-loss reduction versus raw probabilities is 3.0–19.7% across leagues.
Scaling-binning paper reports histogram O(B/epsilon^2), scaling O(1/epsilon^2), scaling-binning O(1/epsilon^2+B), and calibration-error estimation O(sqrt(B)).
Dixon-Coles study uses tuned exponential decay against a margin-free closing market and a logarithmic opinion pool.

methodology_and_algorithms.de_vig_methods: PropLine documents a no-vig fair line for cross-book +EV, with Pinnacle preferred and Bovada fallback; no separate Olympus de-vig formula is confirmed on the assigned methodology page.
methodology_and_algorithms.calibration_ledger_link: Olympus track-record page advertises summary JSON (/webmcp/api/performance), history JSON (/webmcp/api/history), CSV (/track_record.csv), and OpenAPI 3.1 (/openapi.json); these advertised endpoints were not separately crawled under the exact-URL constraint.

published_numbers.track_record: Olympus reports 2,619 resolved picks overall: 52.7% win rate, -9.57u and -0.3% ROI; free segment 1,776 picks, 52.9%, +19.40u, +1.0% ROI; premium 843 picks, 52.3%, -28.97u, -2.6% ROI.
published_numbers.sample_sizes: Olympus Kelly blend validation set: 6,101 games; minimum simulation: 10,000 iterations per scheduled game. PropLine example: 712,043 total graded across 4,120 events over 30 days. Dixon-Coles paper: 7,220 matches over 19 seasons.
published_numbers.clv_records: NOT CONFIRMED as a published CLV record. The Dixon-Coles paper explicitly says a separate CLV statistic is not reported; its benchmark is the closing market.
published_numbers.update_frequency: PropLine advertises live updating every 60 seconds; nflfastR README says complete-season files are updated nightly during the season; ESPN/RotoWire injury endpoint/page update frequencies are NOT CONFIRMED on assigned sources.

prediction_markets.market_schema: Kalshi documentation describes binary yes/no markets, events containing one or more markets, ticker/prices/volume/open-interest, yes/no orderbook bids, trades and settlement rules. Polymarket Gamma market objects expose id/question/conditionId/slug/endDate/outcomes/outcomePrices/volume/liquidity/active/closed; CLOB markets expose data/next_cursor/limit/count and order-book/timestamp/condition/question metadata.

Tiers shown: Hobby 30 days, Pro 90, Streaming Lite 180, Streaming 365, Enterprise unlimited. Snapshots are written only on price/point change; archive starts April 2026.

open_source_and_papers.algorithm_description: nflfastR provides NFL play-by-play and EP/WP/CP/EYAC model outputs; sports-betting combines statistics/odds dataloaders with scikit-learn bettors and backtesting; penaltyblog lists Poisson, bivariate Poisson, Dixon-Coles, Bayesian MCMC/hierarchical models and rating systems; kloppy standardizes provider-specific soccer event/tracking data; the papers cover calibration, pathwise calibration, graph forecasting and Dixon-Coles/closing-market analysis.
